title: fix(superheroes): the review panel reads the session's model from its transcript when the start event omits it
body:
Closes #2110.

## What's changing, and why

When a session's start event did not name the model it runs on (headless builders, and many compact or resume events), the review panel treated the host model as unknown. That made every native Claude reviewer ineligible, so a panel that could have seated Claude dropped it and disclosed `host-model-unknown`, even though the session's own transcript records the model on every turn. Now, when the start event names no model, the panel reads it from the session's own transcript, counting only turns written since this start and never a subagent's. A panel therefore keeps its Claude seats whenever any record of the model exists. A model from an earlier start still never stands in for the live one, and a session the launcher spawns never inherits its parent's model. Review also caught, and this PR fixes, a crash path its first version added: a transcript path that UTF-8 can't encode no longer aborts the session-start hook before it removes the reviewer pass from later shells.

## What we're accepting

- **The bite-proofs were produced by the build orchestrator, not the implementer** (disclosed degradation): the harness refused the implementer's proof command, so the orchestrator ran every proof itself. All eight guarded elements went red with their guard removed and green with it restored. Nothing is unproven.
- **The fixer wrapper differed from the emitted order** (disclosed degradation): the review loop's fixer got its order as a pointer to the driver-emitted file, not as pasted text. The order itself was unchanged.
- **Session 3 has no review record of its own** (disclosed degradation): it converged on `0d21b530`, then a CI-only rename moved the head before its record was written. Session 4 reviewed the final head with a full panel, and its record carries every earlier finding.

## How to see it

N/A, nothing to see: this is review machinery. The change shows only in a review's seat map: no `host-model-unknown` and a known host family when the start event omits the model.

## Advisor vet

<!-- superheroes:advisor-vet -->

**Verdict: NOT-READY** · 58cacc626f18e3183c1f2ae41c51312569876119 (vet 633: the review record and a catch-up with main are owed)

**What was checked.** Both problems from the last vet are fixed. I checked each one myself on this Mac:
- The test that broke on a Mac now passes there. If the bug it guards comes back, the test still fails.
- The reader test now catches a reader that picks an older model over the latest one. Before, that mistake passed every test.
- This round changed tests only; no shipped code changed.
- The other tests this PR touches also pass on the Mac.

**Why it is not ready.**
- The re-check of the fix by an independent reviewer happened, but nothing durable records it. The only trace is a sentence in the builder's comment. The review record, the account every merge rests on, still describes the previous commit.
- Since the PR was built, two other PRs merged and touched the same release-notes file. So the PR can't merge until it catches up with them.

Both are routine. The builder catches up, gets one independent reviewer to read the fix and the catch-up together, writes the record, and hands back. No code changes.

**What accepting it means.** Once that lands: nothing beyond what the PR says. Reviews keep their Claude reviewers when a session's start event leaves the model out. Consuming projects owe nothing. The leftover finding that used to be on your list is fixed, and the new record will say so.

**What is yours to decide.** `None`.

title: fix(superheroes): the review fixer's order says to leave the head-diff keys out
body:
Closes #2109.

## What's changing, and why

The review fixer's order now tells the fixer to leave the two head-diff keys (`headDiff`, `headDiffPath`) out of its result. Before, the order listed them as optional without saying which diff they meant. A fixer that reported its own commit's diff made the driver stop the whole review session (`head-diff-mismatch`), because the driver works out the post-fix diff from git against the review's pinned base and only cross-checks a supplied one. The fixer is never told that base, so it cannot reliably reproduce the driver's diff; leaving the keys out is the one answer that can never stop a round. The driver's cross-check is unchanged.

## What we're accepting

None

## How to see it

N/A — nothing to see: review machinery; the change is one sentence in an order an agent reads.

## Advisor vet
<!-- superheroes:advisor-vet -->

**Verdict: READY** · 6389894d6ddd71d07664eaa1714d90f1db6238d0

**What was checked.** I compared the new instruction with what the review loop actually accepts. The loop works out the fixed code's diff itself and treats any diff a fixer sends only as a check against its own. A diff that doesn't match stops the review, and sending none never does. So "send no diff" is the one instruction a fixer can't get wrong. Both versions of the fixer's instructions now say it. The loop's own check is unchanged. Tests catch the instruction going missing from either version.

**What accepting it means.** The next review fixer stops sending its own diff, so a fix round no longer ends a review session the way it did on #2105. A fixer that ignores the instruction still stops its review loudly. That is the outcome #2109 asked for, and nothing fails quietly. It reaches a review only once a release ships it.

**What is yours to decide.** None.

Full vet: [vet 625 receipt](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/pull/2111#issuecomment-6377320830).

**Carried forward 2026-10-24:** head moved `6389894d` → `858d09b7` by a plain merge of main (after #2093, #2112, #2116, #2101 and #2114 merged), no conflicts; the PR's own changes are unchanged, so the move is not material and the saved Merge carries forward.

**Lane:** light (the advisor's call, recorded in #2109; no escalation trigger fired). Cloud build, plugin 0.45.0, base `170f3705a911a480a27031e9beb9afdb4fd112ad`. The PR was opened as a draft so the review record had a PR to write against, and marked ready at handback.

### The design call (the issue left it to the builder)

Tell the fixer to **leave both keys out**, rather than say what they must hold. Why: in a run with a repository the driver always derives the diff from git (`_fold_fixer`, `round_driver.py`), so an omitted diff reads `headDiffCheck: none-supplied` and never parks; a supplied one can only match or stop the round. The fixer is not told the pinned base, so "what they must hold" would ask it to reproduce `git diff <base>...<head>` byte-for-byte from a base it doesn't know. In a run with no repository (the eval/replay path), an omitted diff reads as an unknown surface and escalates to a full panel: fail-closed, costlier, never wrong.

**Where the rule lives:** the rendered step-5 block (`FIXER_NO_HEAD_DIFF_RULE`, appended in `_fixer_derived_placeholders` in `plugins/superheroes/lib/round_orders.py`), for both the host-seat and the engine-seat renders. It cannot go in `rubric/orders/dispatch-fixer.md` itself: `test_template_body_does_not_restate_payload_contract` forbids naming payload fields in a template body, and weakening that census (its `exempt_fields` hook) was rejected.

### Features

* **superheroes:** a vet-drafter agent lets the advisor vet several PRs in parallel ([#2112](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/issues/2112)) ([384bc3c](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/commit/384bc3c5371264d6764fc0406676ca4bf57919b9))

* **superheroes:** readiness, the cloud check and the setup text read the plugin pin ([#2042](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/issues/2042)) ([b1b5c4b](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/commit/b1b5c4b4281b76488476d34224933298b8d118fd))
